walkthroughs.body_html: Freud (1896-1939) argued behaviour arises from unconscious conflict between id, ego and superego. Five psychosexual stages; fixation at any stage shapes adult character. Case study Little Hans (1909) used phobia to argue for Oedipus complex. Approach criticised as unfalsifiable.

Maslow (1943)'s hierarchy: physiological, safety, love, esteem, self-actualisation. Rogers (1959): people are intrinsically good and growth-motivated. Therapy provides unconditional positive regard to restore congruence between actual and ideal self.

Psychodynamic explains development, depression and dreams but is hard to test scientifically. Humanistic celebrates free will and offers usable therapy but is hard to measure (the Q-sort partially fixes this). Both emphasise subjective experience over lab control.
